    StartersKnuckles's marmalade sandwichesSeville orange marmalade boiled from scratch, spread on buttered breadHow to make it500g Seville oranges1.2 L water1kg caster sugar1 lemon8 slices of white bread80g butterSimmer the whole oranges in the water until soft.Halve, scoop out the pips and shred the peel.Return to the liquid with the sugar and lemon juice and boil hard to 105°C.Jar and cool.Butter the bread thickly, spread with marmalade and cut into triangles.Prison kitchen leek and potato soupThick leek and potato soup in tin mugs, with buttered toast soldiersHow to make it40g butter3 leeks, sliced1 onion, diced600g potatoes, diced1 L vegetable stock150ml thickened cream8 slices of white bread1 bunch chivesMelt the butter in a large pot and cook the leeks and onion gently for 10 minutes without colouring.Add the potatoes and stock and simmer 20 minutes until soft.Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season.Toast and butter the bread and cut into soldiers.Serve the soup in mugs with snipped chives and the soldiers.Hot lineDish of the day: bear pie (it's chicken)Chicken, leek and mushroom in a creamy Dijon sauce under pastryHow to make it800g chicken thighs, diced2 leeks250g mushrooms60g butter2 tbsp plain flour250ml chicken stock200ml thickened cream1 tsp Dijon mustard1 bunch thyme1 sheet puff pastry1 egg300g frozen peasBrown the chicken in some of the butter, then add the sliced leeks and mushrooms and soften.Stir in the flour, then the stock, cream, Dijon and thyme and simmer until thick.Cool, tip into a pie dish, top with puff pastry and brush with egg.Bake at 200°C until golden.Toss the peas in the remaining butter and serve alongside.Funfair sausage and onion rollsThick pork snags grilled sticky, buttery onions and English mustard, before sauce.Cook 3 sliced onions in 40g butter with a pinch of brown sugar over low heat for 25 minutes until soft and golden.Grill 8 thick pork sausages over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning often,
